userStories.title: Inject direction stack, MEMORY.md, and installed skills into Quick Run spec generation prompt
userStories.description: The POST /api/pipeline/quick-run route in backend/src/routes/pipeline.ts generates a 1-story spec at step 7 using a bare LLM call (quickRunPrompt) with no workspace context. The prompt only receives the user's brief. This means the generated spec is context-blind — it does not know the project's tech stack, engineering conventions, past decisions, or available skills. Fix this by injecting the same context that POST /api/specs/generate uses: the synthesized direction stack (L1–L3), the first 2000 chars of MEMORY.md (if present), and a list of installed skill names+descriptions.
acceptanceCriteria: Before building quickRunPrompt, call synthesize(workspaceId, workspace.domain) from backend/src/lib/direction-stack.ts. Import synthesize at the top of pipeline.ts if not already imported. Store the result as directionContext. If synthesize throws or returns empty string, set directionContext to empty string and continue (non-fatal).

Read MEMORY.md from path.join(workspace.path, 'MEMORY.md') using fs.readFileSync with 'utf-8' encoding wrapped in a try/catch. If the file exists and has content, take the first 2000 characters as memoryContext. If missing or empty, set memoryContext to empty string.

Query installed skills: SELECT name, description FROM skill_files WHERE workspace_id = $1 OR workspace_id IS NULL LIMIT 20 — if that table does not exist, fall back to reading the .rorca/skills/ directory (fs.readdirSync(path.join(workspace.path, '.rorca', 'skills'))) and listing filenames without extension. Build skillsContext as a plain-text list 'name: description' (one per line). If no skills, set skillsContext to empty string.

Prepend context blocks to quickRunPrompt as follows: if directionContext is non-empty, prepend '=== DIRECTION STACK (follow these conventions) ===
' + directionContext + '

'. If memoryContext is non-empty, prepend '=== PROJECT MEMORY (past decisions and patterns) ===
' + memoryContext + '

'. If skillsContext is non-empty, prepend '=== INSTALLED SKILLS (reference these when relevant) ===
' + skillsContext + '

'. All three blocks go BEFORE the existing '=== INSTRUCTIONS: READ THIS FIRST ===' section.

Change the acceptance criteria cap from 5 to 8: update the comment '// Enforce single story + max 5 AC' to max 8, and update the slice to story.acceptanceCriteria.slice(0, 8). Update the rule in quickRunPrompt from 'The story must have at most 5 acceptance criteria' to 'at most 8 acceptance criteria'.
After the change, run cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit from the repo root — zero new type errors must be introduced in pipeline.ts.

The context injection is non-blocking: if synthesize(), fs.readFileSync(), or the skills query throws, catch the error, log it with console.warn, and proceed with empty context strings. Quick Run must never fail due to context injection errors.
